messages:
Dmitry: Ran a perf sweep on mixtral-8k canary this morning. Seeing intermittent 120-200ms token spikes when user prompts include emoji or rare unicode sequences. Root cause looks like kernel selector flipping to a slower path.
Erin: ugh, emoji again. can you paste the profiler output?
Dmitry: snippet from trace: 
```
kernel_picker stats: fast_attn: 97.3%
byte_compat_kernel: 2.7% (spikes correlate with requests containing non-ascii)
kv_cache: hit_rate=98.6%
kv_warmup_missburst: 1.4% (aligned with spikes)
latency_p50=12ms p95=36ms p99=210ms
```

Carla: that p99 is from those fallback picks. byte_compat_kernel is not optimized for cached KV layout, so it nukes the fast path.
Ben: is tokenizer doing byte-fallback per token or per input? we've seen different behaviors across qwen/mixtral/llama.
Dmitry: tokenizer emits a byte-fallback token when encountering certain control chars. For these prompts the total token count goes up by ~7-12 tokens which expands seq_len and pushes kernel_picker into conservative mode.
Alice: could be RoPE scaling too. Mixtral profile shows head_dim mismatch heuristics trigger a safer kernel when scale factor != 1.0.
Erin: do we have a quick repro? need a minimal prompt that causes fallback without real PII.
Dmitry: repro: "Hey 🤖 please summarize:
1) \u200b
2) \u2060" (zero-width + word-joiner combination). Running that on mixtral-8k triggers byte path 3/10 runs.
Carla: thanks. can we try forcing kernel_picker.prefer_rope_optimized=true on canary? might avoid fallback if issue is RoPE heuristic.
Ben: quick config suggestion to test: 
```
runtime:
  kernel_picker:
    prefer_rope_optimized: true
    batch_timeout_ms: 8
    max_batch_tokens: 8192
tokenizer:
  byte_fallback_threshold: 6
```
Will try on canary.
Erin: note batch_timeout_ms bump can trade latency-> fewer SLO breaches. keep an eye on p50.
infra-bot: deploy started for canary: mixtral-8k / config bump (id: cb-2026-03-18-1) :rocket:
Dmitry: after deploy: p99 spike rate dropped ~60% but p50 increased by 4ms. KV_missburst still present at 0.6% for these prompts.
Carla: interesting. so prefer_rope_optimized helped kernel choice but didn't fully eliminate warmup. probably cache warmup because tokenization expanded length unpredictably.
Ben: idea: add a short prefix normalization step to strip zero-widths and normalize emoji to NFKC for inference route. That would reduce byte fallbacks.
Alice: caution: normalization can change semantics for some customers. we should gate it per-route or add as an opt-in preprocessing rule.
Erin: what about batching heuristics? If these prompts are short we can enable a tiny prefix-caching window so subsequent requests reuse KV without warmup. e.g., kv_prefetch_ms=20 for routes with chat-template style prompts.
Dmitry: ran a micro-benchmark toggling kv_prefetch_ms: 0/10/20/50 ms. 20ms gave best tradeoff: reduced warmup spikes by ~35% with marginal cost.
Carla: can someone share the perf command you used? I'll re-run across qwen/mistral/llama.
Dmitry: command: `perf_profile --model mixtral-8k --trace kernels,kv --tokenize --sample 1000 --out /tmp/mixtral_trace.json`
Ben: results on qwen-7b: tokenization produces fewer byte-fallback tokens, kernel_picker stayed on fast_attn 99.8% — suggests tokenizer differences are major factor.
Alice: for Llama-2 13B we see RoPE scaling factor being applied at compile-time; if compile-time scale != runtime expectation it forces kernel fallback. double-check compile flags.
Carla: action items: 1) add per-route token normalization opt-in (Ben) 2) run compile-flag audit for RoPE across models (Alice) 3) add kv_prefetch_ms=20 as an experiment for chat routes (Erin) 4) add a lightweight profiler alert when byte_compat_kernel > 0.5% (Dmitry)
Erin: I'll prepare a small dashboard: kernel-picker heatmap by route + tokenizer fallback rate.
infra-bot: task created: INF-5234 (canary config experiment) assigned to Erin, due 2026-03-22.
Ben: one more thought — batching heuristics: current max_batch_tokens enforcement is conservative for long-context chat templates. If we allow per-route max_batch_tokens increase for verified routes we can avoid kernel demotion caused by sequence fragmentation.
Dmitry: agreed. we should be careful with memory spikes. maybe a soft quota that signals the kernel_picker but doesn't immediately fallback.
Carla: good convo. I'll run cross-model sweep tonight and post results. thanks :thumbsup:
summary: Short thread discussing mixtral canary perf spikes caused by tokenizer byte-fallback, kernel picker fallback to slower kernel, RoPE scaling and KV warmup. Team agrees on canary config changes (prefer_rope_optimized, batch_timeout_ms, kv_prefetch_ms) and opt-in token normalization; infra tasks created.
